data.name: Thorn
data.gender_notes: Thorn is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'thornos' meaning 'a protective hedge'. In Christian symbolism, the thorn represents the Passion of Christ and the suffering He endured for humanity. The name Thorn carries the meaning “Prickly, Protective” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Thorn usually hope their child will grow to embody prickly, protective and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of protection, endurance, and sacrifice.
data.etymology: Thorn belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Prickly, Protective.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Thorn total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: עצמות
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The name Thorn in Hebrew is derived from the word עצמות (atzmot), meaning 'sharp point'. In the Bible, this name is associated with the thorn in the side of Jesus Christ (John 19:2).

in_greek.name: ακανθα
in_greek.long_meaning: The name Thorn in Greek is ακανθα (akantha), meaning 'thorn'. In the Bible, this name is used in various passages to refer to physical thorns or metaphorical suffering (2 Corinthians 12:7).

in_latin.name: spinas
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Thorn in Latin is spinas, meaning 'thorn'. In the Bible, this name is used to describe various thorns and thorny plants, as well as symbolic suffering (Matthew 7:16).

in_english.name: Thorn
in_english.long_meaning: The name Thorn in English is derived from Old English thorn, meaning 'thorn'. In the Bible, this name is used to refer to various thorns and thorny plants, as well as metaphorical suffering (Exodus 3:8).

data.cultural_impact: The name Thorn brings to mind the story of Christ's crucifixion and the crown of thorns placed on His head. This name has been used throughout history, with prominent figures like St. Theodore the Great Martyr, St. Thorn of Cornwall, and St. Thorn of Pavia. The name evokes a sense of resilience and strength in the face of adversity and suffering.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Thorn serves as a reminder of Christ's sacrifices and the importance of enduring suffering with faith and grace. It encourages us to embrace the challenges and hardships of life with a humble and steadfast spirit, and to seek the strength and wisdom that comes from trusting in God during difficult times.

biblical_reference.note: In the Bible, the name Thorn is first mentioned in the book of Exodus, where God commands Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egypt and promises to bring them to a land flowing with milk and honey. He warns Moses that the people will not believe him and will ask for a sign, so God tells Moses to cast his staff on the ground, and it will become a thorn bush (עצמות, atzmot). When Moses strikes the water of the Nile with his staff, all the waters are turned into blood (Exodus 7:20).
